title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #3

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #3
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does the word indigenous mean? (1 mark)
   A. Brought from another continent
   B. Belonging to a people and place from long ago
   C. Very new
   D. Made in a factory

2. What is the job of the ropes on a drum? (1 mark)
   A. To decorate the beater
   B. To make the shell heavy
   C. To make the drum float
   D. To hold the skin tight

3. What is the correct order for making charcoal sticks? (1 mark)
   A. Trim, cool, burn, cut
   B. Cool, burn, trim, cut
   C. Cut, trim, burn, cool
   D. Burn, cut, trim, cool

4. When accompanying singers, the drummers should (1 mark)
   A. stop at every line
   B. play softly enough for the singers to be heard
   C. shout the words
   D. play as loud as possible

5. Smudging a charcoal drawing means (1 mark)
   A. painting over it
   B. rubbing it gently so the tones blend
   C. erasing it completely
   D. folding the paper

6. What is charcoal? (1 mark)
   A. Black carbon left when wood is heated with little air
   B. A kind of wet paint
   C. Ground chalk
   D. A type of clay

7. The basic knot for the macramé ball is the (1 mark)
   A. sailor's knot
   B. reef knot
   C. overhand knot
   D. fisherman's bend

8. How many players are in a full netball team on the court? (1 mark)
   A. 11
   B. 9
   C. 7
   D. 5

9. Red mixed with yellow makes (1 mark)
   A. orange
   B. green
   C. purple
   D. brown

10. Which colour is a secondary colour? (1 mark)
   A. Red
   B. Blue
   C. Green
   D. Yellow

11. What is the theme of the montage in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Ball games
   B. Weather
   C. Food
   D. Wild animals

12. Which letter has a descender? (1 mark)
   A. a
   B. e
   C. g
   D. k

13. The French rhythm name for a pair of quavers is (1 mark)
   A. taa
   B. rest
   C. ta-te
   D. tee-taa

14. The middle note of d, r and m is (1 mark)
   A. none
   B. m
   C. d
   D. r

15. How many notes are in the melody d r m m r d? (1 mark)
   A. Five
   B. Six
   C. Three
   D. Four

16. Why should the flag stick be held high when cheering? (1 mark)
   A. So it does not hit anyone
   B. To make noise
   C. To hide the runners
   D. To block the sun

17. In a crab balance, your fingers point (1 mark)
   A. behind your back
   B. away from your feet
   C. towards your feet
   D. up to the sky

18. Which muscles does the crab balance mainly strengthen? (1 mark)
   A. Only the fingers
   B. Only the ears
   C. Only the eyes
   D. Arms, shoulders, tummy and legs

19. Why is gymnastics described as not being a race? (1 mark)
   A. It is about control and quality, not speed
   B. It is always in the dark
   C. It uses no body
   D. It cannot be seen

20. Which folk songs are sung while working? (1 mark)
   A. Marriage songs
   B. Naming songs
   C. Work songs
   D. Funeral songs

21. In music, the sign f means (1 mark)
   A. slow
   B. loud
   C. silent
   D. soft

22. Which facial expression fits a joyful song? (1 mark)
   A. A smile
   B. A yawn
   C. A frown
   D. Closed eyes

23. The message of a song is (1 mark)
   A. the number of singers
   B. the name of the drum
   C. the colour of the stage
   D. the main idea the singers want us to hear

24. Early morning and late afternoon light is (1 mark)
   A. harsh
   B. soft and gentle
   C. too dark always
   D. absent

25. To keep the camera steady you should (1 mark)
   A. hold it with both hands and keep elbows near your body
   B. shake it
   C. hold it at arm's length with one finger
   D. throw it

26. How should you hold a camera or tablet? (1 mark)
   A. By the lens
   B. With both hands
   C. By one corner
   D. Over your head

27. The battery of a camera (1 mark)
   A. keeps it dry
   B. takes the photo
   C. gives it power
   D. cleans the lens

28. A blurred photograph is (1 mark)
   A. always good
   B. very clear
   C. not sharp
   D. dark

29. To make the centre of interest clearer you can (1 mark)
   A. shake the camera
   B. move very far away
   C. add lots of clutter
   D. move closer to the subject

30. A descant recorder is made of (1 mark)
   A. glass
   B. metal foil only
   C. plastic or wood
   D. paper only

31. Of the notes B, A and G, which is the lowest? (1 mark)
   A. B
   B. A
   C. G
   D. They are equal

32. Covering more finger holes makes the note (1 mark)
   A. louder always
   B. lower
   C. silent
   D. higher

33. Which note is played with the thumb and holes 1, 2 and 3 covered? (1 mark)
   A. A
   B. F
   C. B
   D. G

34. Which float has the body curled up like a ball? (1 mark)
   A. Glide
   B. Mushroom float
   C. Prone float
   D. Supine float

35. Where should beginners stay in the pool? (1 mark)
   A. The shallow end
   B. The deep end
   C. Wherever
   D. Under a diving board

36. In the frog jump, you begin (1 mark)
   A. sitting
   B. standing on one leg
   C. lying flat
   D. in a squat with your hands on the ground

37. How does the hawk tag? (1 mark)
   A. By pushing
   B. By pulling clothes
   C. By tripping
   D. Gently on the back or shoulders

38. When someone comments on your work, you should (1 mark)
   A. tear the work
   B. listen quietly and say thank you
   C. argue
   D. walk away

39. Verse 3 of the anthem talks about (1 mark)
   A. the weather
   B. sports
   C. working together to build the nation and giving thanks
   D. cooking

40. A good sportsperson (1 mark)
   A. cheats
   B. quits
   C. congratulates winners and encourages losers
   D. argues with the referee

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Where do the notes B, A and G sit on the staff? (3 marks)

42. Explain how animal games help to keep the body healthy. (4 marks)

43. State four things you would look for when appreciating a sports performance. (4 marks)

44. How can you show that you have identified the pitch of a note by ear? (3 marks)

45. Explain what is meant by two stars and a wish in feedback. (3 marks)

46. State four safety rules for gymnastics. (4 marks)

47. Explain the job of the drumhead and the shell of a drum. (3 marks)

48. Describe the correct posture and hand position for playing the recorder. (4 marks)

49. Describe how to present an artwork from your portfolio. (4 marks)

50. Why do we scratch and wet clay before joining pieces? (3 marks)

51. Describe how to make a montage on ball games. (4 marks)

52. Give four ways to make a clear centre of interest. (4 marks)

53. What is the East African Community? (3 marks)

54. Describe how to make a portfolio from manila paper. (5 marks)

55. Why should we take turns and respect others' views when talking about paintings and montages? (3 marks)

56. State two ways to keep the working area clean after painting. (2 marks)

57. Explain how to compose a short melody using d, r and m. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #3 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Belonging to a people and place from long ago
   Indigenous instruments belong to a community and were made from local materials.

2. D — To hold the skin tight
   Ropes or lacing keep the skin stretched tight.

3. C — Cut, trim, burn, cool
   The stages are cutting, trimming, burning, then cooling.

4. B — play softly enough for the singers to be heard
   Accompaniment supports the singers and must not cover their voices.

5. B — rubbing it gently so the tones blend
   Smudging spreads the charcoal so that light and dark blend smoothly.

6. A — Black carbon left when wood is heated with little air
   Charcoal is the black carbon left after wood is burned with very little air.

7. C — overhand knot
   The learner uses overhand knots to make the net around the core.

8. C — 7
   A full netball team has seven players on court.

9. A — orange
   Red and yellow together give orange.

10. C — Green
   Green is made from yellow and blue.

11. A — Ball games
   The montage is themed ball games.

12. C — g
   The tail of g goes below the baseline.

13. C — ta-te
   Ta-te is two short sounds in one beat.

14. D — r
   Ray lies between doh and me.

15. B — Six
   Count d, r, m, m, r, d to get six.

16. A — So it does not hit anyone
   Keeping it high and away from the track avoids hitting people.

17. C — towards your feet
   In the crab position, hands are behind you with fingers pointing to the feet.

18. D — Arms, shoulders, tummy and legs
   Holding the body up uses many muscle groups.

19. A — It is about control and quality, not speed
   Skill and control matter more than speed.

20. C — Work songs
   Work songs give rhythm to work.

21. B — loud
   The letter f stands for loud.

22. A — A smile
   Facial expressions show the mood.

23. D — the main idea the singers want us to hear
   Message is the main idea.

24. B — soft and gentle
   These times give soft light.

25. A — hold it with both hands and keep elbows near your body
   A steady hold gives a sharp photograph.

26. B — With both hands
   Two hands prevent dropping.

27. C — gives it power
   Without power the device will not work.

28. C — not sharp
   Blurred means not sharp.

29. D — move closer to the subject
   Getting closer helps the subject fill the picture.

30. C — plastic or wood
   Recorders are commonly made of plastic or wood.

31. C — G
   More holes covered gives a lower note.

32. B — lower
   More holes covered gives a longer air column, so a lower note.

33. D — G
   G adds the third hole.

34. B — Mushroom float
   The tucked body with the back at the surface is the mushroom float.

35. A — The shallow end
   Shallow water is safer.

36. D — in a squat with your hands on the ground
   You squat and spring forward.

37. D — Gently on the back or shoulders
   Gentle tagging keeps everyone safe.

38. B — listen quietly and say thank you
   Good listeners grow.

39. C — working together to build the nation and giving thanks
   It calls for common effort and gratitude.

40. C — congratulates winners and encourages losers
   Fair play and respect.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: B is on line 3, A is in the space between line 2 and line 3, and G is on line 2.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: They strengthen muscles, stretch the body, improve balance and coordination and make the heart and lungs stronger.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Teamwork, skill, safety and sportsmanship.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen to the note, decide if it is low, middle or high, and make the hand sign for it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for listening, 1 mark for deciding pitch, 1 mark for hand sign.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say two good things about the work and then give one suggestion for improvement.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Use a mat or soft ground; keep the space clear; remove jewellery; tie back long hair; warm up; take turns; stop if there is pain. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: The drumhead vibrates when struck and makes the sound. The hollow shell makes the sound fuller and louder.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the drumhead, 2 marks for the shell's job explained.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sit or stand tall. Hold the recorder pointing down and away. The left hand is at the top and the right hand at the bottom. The left thumb covers the thumb hole and fingers cover holes with the pads.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Hold it carefully, say the title, explain the materials and skills, tell the message, say what you like and what you would change, and listen to feedback.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: It makes the surface rough and sticky so the pieces hold together and do not fall off when dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for scratching, 1 mark for water, 1 mark for the reason.

51. (4 marks)
   Answer: Collect and cut pictures of ball games from old papers. Arrange them on a background without gluing, overlapping the pieces. Paste the back ones first and then the others. Add a title and let it dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decide the subject first; move closer; remove distractions; place the subject in the middle or slightly to the side; keep it sharp; bend to eye level. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: A group of countries in East Africa that work together on matters such as trade, travel and peace.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for group of countries, 1 mark for East Africa, 1 mark for working together.

54. (5 marks)
   Answer: Fold two large pieces of manila paper to make a folder and trim the edges. Punch holes and add a string tie. Paste coloured paper or fabric on the cover. Write a label with name and class. Put in the works with dates and notes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of the five parts.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is fair, it shows respect and it helps everyone learn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: Wash the brushes and containers, wipe the desk, put the paper in the bin. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a rhythm. Give a syllable to each note. Use steps. End on d as a crotchet. Sing it and show the hand signs. Write the syllables under the rhythm names.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.
